stories.title: Governance Authority - retrieving a list of all schemas metadata via API
stories.status: DevTeam PBI is ready for Implementation check

user_story.i want: to retrieve a list of all schemas metadata available in the system via API,
user_story.so that: I can get a high-level overview of all registered schemas.

clauses.text: I am an API client with a valid authentication token granting the `GA_SCHEMA_VIEWER` or `GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN` role.
I send a `GET` request to the `/schemas` endpoint.
the service shall respond with a *200 OK* HTTP status.
the response body shall contain a paginated list of schemas (20 items / page by default, see pagination guidelines).
each resource in the list shall include all the relevant metadata.
I am an API client with a valid authentication token granting the `GA_SCHEMA_VIEWER` or `GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN` role.
I send a `GET` request to the `/schemas` endpoint with the supported query parameters
the service shall respond with a *200 OK* HTTP status.
the response body shall contain a paginated list of schemas that match the provided filter criteria.
I am an API client without a valid authentication token,
I send a `GET` request to the `/schemas` endpoint,
the service shall respond with a `401 Unauthorized` HTTP status.
I am an API client with a valid authentication token but without the required `governance-viewer` or `governance-admin` role,
I send a `GET` request to the `/schemas` endpoint,
the service shall respond with a `403 Forbidden` HTTP status.
I am an API client with a valid authentication token,
I send a `GET` request to the `/schemas` endpoint with an invalid query parameter (e.g., `?status=INVALID_STATUS`),
the service shall respond with a `400 Bad Request` HTTP status.
the response body should contain a problem details JSON object explaining the error.

stories.title: Governance Authority - retrieving metadata for all versions of a schema via API
stories.status: Ready for DG Acceptance

user_story.i want: to retrieve a list of all available versions for a specific schema via API,
user_story.so that: I can review its entire version history, change logs, and metadata.

clauses.text: I am an API client with a valid authentication token granting the `GA_SCHEMA_VIEWER or GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN` role.
I have the unique name of an existing schema (e.g., `InfrastructureSchema`).
I send a `GET` request to the `/schemas/{schemaName}/versions` endpoint.
the service shall respond with a `200 OK` HTTP status.
the response body must be a paginated list of schema versions (20 items/page by default - see pagination guidelines [https://www.belgif.be/specification/rest/api-guide/#pagination])
each schema version in the list must include all its metadata
I am an API client with a valid and authorized token.

I send a `GET` request to `/schemas/{schemaName}/versions` where {schemaName} contains illegal characters (e.g., `Infrastructure$chema!`). (Schema name must be `PascalCase`. Alphanumeric only. Min 3, Max 64 chars. No spaces or special characters.)
the service shall respond with a `400 Bad Request` HTTP status.
the response body should contain a descriptive error message about the invalid format.
I am an API client with a valid authentication token granting the `GA_SCHEMA_VIEWER` role.
I have a schema name that is correctly formatted but does not exist in the system (e.g., "UnknownSchema").
I send a `GET` request to the `/schemas/UnknownSchema/versions` endpoint.
the service shall respond with a `404 Not Found` HTTP status.

I have navigated to the details page for a specific schema (e.g., "Application resource schema").
the schema versions page loads,
the UI shall call the backend `GET /schemas/{schemaName}/versions` endpoint to retrieve all versions for that schema.
the UI shall display a table listing each version with its **Version** number, *Status*, *Creation Date*, *Creator*, and **Latest Change** (changelog).

stories.title: Governance Authority - retrieving the contents of the latest version of a schema via API
stories.status: Ready for DG Acceptance

user_story.i want: to: Retrieve the raw SHACL content of the latest published version of a schema by making a request to a stable, public, unversioned URI

clauses.text: I am an authenticated GA user,
a schema concept (e.g., ApplicationAsset) exists in the system.
the ApplicationAsset schema has a version (e.g., "1.0.0", "1.1.0", "1.2.0"), with "1.2.0" being the latest.
I send a GET request to the endpoint for the schema concept, for example, [https://api.simpl.space/schemas/ApplicationAsset].
the service shall identify "1.2.0" as the latest version.
the service shall respond directly with a 200 OK HTTP status.

the response shall include a Content-Location header that specifies the versioned URI of the content being served (e.g., Content-Location: [https://api.simpl.space/schemas/ApplicationAsset/1.2.0]), which is also the named graph of the schema.
the response shall have a Content-Type header of text/turtle.
the body of the response shall contain the complete, raw SHACL content of version "1.2.0".

acs.label: AC2

clauses.text: I am an authenticated GA client,
I send a GET request to the Resolver Interface endpoint for a schema name that does not exist, such as [https://api.simpl.space/schemas/NonExistentSchema].
the service shall respond with a 404 Not Found HTTP status.

other_text: As this is not a REST API we don't need an API Definition task for it:
- we don't need versioning (it's the schemas that are versioned)
- we don't need any custom headers or request params that would involve having a REST API

stories.title: Governance Authority – providing details of a new schema via an API
stories.status: DevTeam PBI is ready for Implementation check

user_story.i want: to submit the definition for a new schema by providing its core metadata and its initial SHACL content via a single API call,
user_story.so that: I can have the system create the schema concept and automatically establish its first version as 1.0.0.

clauses.text: I am an API client authenticated with the GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN role,
I have the required metadata for the new schema concept (e.g., {"name": "DataAsset", "title": "Data Asset", "description": "Describes a discoverable dataset.", "resourceType": "data"}).
I have a valid SHACL schema definition saved in a .ttl file.
I send a POST request to the /api/v1/schemas endpoint with the .ttl file and the JSON metadata as multipart/form-data.
the Schema Management Service (SMS) shall validate the syntax and integrity of the submitted SHACL file.
if validation is successful, the service shall create a new schema concept using the provided metadata.
the service shall automatically create an initial schema version with versionInfo set to "1.0.0" (with a default changelog like "Initial version.") and store the submitted SHACL file as its content.
the service shall respond with a 201 Created HTTP status and include a Location header pointing to the URI of the newly created schema concept resource.
I am an API client authenticated with the GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN role,
I have metadata for a new schema.
a schema with the same name as in the metadata already exists in the system.
I send a POST request to /api/v1/schemas with the schema metadata and a valid SHACL file.
the service shall respond with a 409 Conflict HTTP status.
the service shall not create a new schema concept or version.

acs.label: AC3

clauses.text: I am an API client authenticated with the GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN role,
I have metadata for a new schema.
I have a SHACL schema definition file that contains syntax errors.
I send a POST request to /api/v1/schemas with the invalid .ttl file and the JSON metadata.
the service shall respond with a 400 Bad Request HTTP status.
the response body shall contain a structured error message detailing the validation failure.
the service shall not create a new schema concept or version.

other_text: * we don't specifically handle semantic validation in this story, if we can store the info in the persistence layer (Fuseki2) that's the syntax and integrity check

the response body contains the full resource metadata representation of the new version.

the schema with name `{nonExistantSchemaName}` doesn't exist
I send a `POST` request to `/schemas/{nonExistentSchemaName}/versions`,
the service shall respond with a `404 Not Found` HTTP status.

a version number of it: `{schemaVersion}` that already exists
I send a `POST` request to `/schemas/{schemaName}/versions` with version number `{schemaVersion}`,

the response body shall contain a problem details JSON object explaining the version conflict.
I am an API client with a valid authentication token granting the `GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN` role,
I have an invalid SHACL file
correct metadata (e.g. version, schemaName)
I send a `POST` request to `/schemas/{schemaName}/versions` with said file
the service shall respond with a `400 Bad Request` HTTP status,
the response body shall contain a problem details JSON object explaining the validation error.
I am an API client with a valid authentication token granting the `GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN` role,
I have a valid SHACL file
malformed metadata (e.g., invalid version format, missing changelog),
I send a `POST` request to `/schemas/{schemaName}/versions` with said SHACL file and metadata
the service shall respond with a `400 Bad Request` HTTP status,
the response body shall contain a problem details JSON object explaining the validation error.
I am an authenticated API client
an unexpected server-side error occurs while processing the request
the system must return Internal Server Error

other_text: Technical Info: Important links to start to develop or helpful data.

Semantic validation is the overall validation process that ensures the schema is meaningful and consistent with the vocabularies it references. Validation rules, relationships, and dependencies are the specific checks performed as part of semantic validation:
* checking that referenced vocabularies and vocabulary terms exist
* checking that schema properties use allowed vocabulary terms
* checking that property relationships are valid
* checking that dependencies between properties are satisfied
* checking that constraints defined by the referenced vocabularies are respected
* we can only validate against self managed vocabularies as it wouldn't be safe to fetch external vocabularies
* we issue warnings for external vocabularies that cannot be resolved
* when doing semantic validation don't fail on first issue - perform a full semantic validation and return all semantic errors
Enforcement of validation rules, relationships, and dependencies is part of semantic validation.

stories.title: [API Implementation] - API to manage federated Search Schema
stories.status: DevTeam PBI In Progress

user_story.i want: the Schema Manager to manage Federated Search schemas
user_story.so that: I can enable federated search across data spaces using a validated common schema without disrupting existing resource-schema clients.

acs.label: AC1
acs.heading: AC1: Create and validate a Federated Search schema

clauses.text: I am authenticated as a Governance Authority user with a role authorising schema management
there is no published (not revoked) Federated Search schema
I create a new Federated Search schema or a new version of it with `schemaType=SEARCH`
Simpl-Open successfully validates the submitted schema according to the rules and default properties for `SEARCH`
Simpl-Open generates the version number using the versioning algorithm
Simpl-Open publish the schema or schema version

acs.label: AC2
acs.heading: AC2: Publish a Federated Search schema

clauses.text: I am authenticated as a Governance Authority user with a role authorising schema management
there is already a published Federated Search schema
I create a new Federated Search schema
Simpl-Open rejects the attempt with `409 Conflict`.

acs.label: AC3
acs.heading: AC3: Filter the schema list by schema type

clauses.text: I am authenticated as a Governance Authority user with a role authorising schema viewing
I retrieve schemas through `GET /schemas` with `schemaType=SEARCH`
Simpl returns only the schemas that match the requested schema type
each returned schema includes its `schemaType`.
if the request also includes `resourceType`, Simpl returns `400 Bad Request`.

acs.label: AC4
acs.heading: AC4: Filter Federated Search schema content and versions by schema type

clauses.text: I am authenticated as a Governance Authority user with a role authorising schema viewing
I retrieve a Federated Search schema's latest content, a specific schema version, or all versions of a schema with `schemaType=SEARCH`
Simpl returns only the matching schema or schema versions
the latest-version and version-specific endpoints return the complete raw SHACL content for the matching schema version.

acs.label: AC5
acs.heading: AC5: Revoke a Federated Search schema

clauses.text: I am authenticated as a Governance Authority user with a role authorising schema management
I revoke the published Federated Search schema
the GET endpoint on the respective federated schema shows that the schema is revoked.
after revocation, a valid Federated Search schema can be published.

bp_requirements.title: Create a new schema
bp_requirements.text: The _Governance Authority_ creates the schema by providing a comprehensive and structured definition, detailing its custom mandatory and custom recommended properties, data types, constraints, validation rules, and any relationships or dependencies.

bp_requirements.title: Create a new version of the schema
bp_requirements.text: The _Governance Authority_ selects an existing schema from the data space catalogue. The _Governance Authority_ creates the new version of the schema by providing a comprehensive and structured definition, detailing its custom mandatory and custom recommended properties, data types, constraints, validation rules, and any relationships or dependencies.

bp_requirements.title: Revoke a schema
bp_requirements.text: The _Governance Authority_ revokes an existing schema if it becomes obsolete, superseded, or no longer relevant to the data space.

bp_requirements.title: Validate the schema
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open enriches the schema with default properties, then validates through: - Syntactic validation according to imposed structure and formatting. - Semantic validation of schema properties based on vocabularies used.

bp_requirements.title: Publish the schema
bp_requirements.text: Upon successful validation, the new schema or new version of an existing schema is published in the data space catalogue. If it concerns the creation of a new version of an existing schema, the previous version is revoked.

bp_requirements.title: Inform Providers about changes of the schema
bp_requirements.text: _Providers_ are notified about changes (e.g. via email).

bp_requirements.title: Send report
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open sends a report to the _Governance Authority_ about validation issues of the schema.

bp_requirements.title: Governance Authority - retrieving schemas and their versions
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open shall allow the retrieval of schemas and their versions, enabling the Governance Authority to review them and take action.

bp_requirements.title: Governance Authority - creating a new schema
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open shall allow the Governance Authority to create a schema, so that resource descriptions created from it align with the standards and rules defined by the Governance Authority for its data space, and so that advanced search contains properties relevant for the selected catalogues during search. This applies to federated search.

bp_requirements.title: Governance Authority - creating a new version of an existing schema
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open shall enable the Governance Authority to create a new version of an existing schema, so that resource descriptions created from the new version align with the standards and rules defined by the Governance Authority for its data space.

bp_requirements.title: Governance Authority - validating a schema
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open shall allow the Governance Authority to syntactically and semantically validate a schema. This includes verifying the structural correctness of the schema as well as ensuring the semantic integrity of its properties against the vocabularies used to define them. The validation process shall also confirm that Simpl's default properties are correctly applied, ensuring consistency with Simpl governance rules.

bp_requirements.title: Governance Authority - receiving feedback about schema validation issues
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open shall provide feedback to the Governance Authority about the validation issues of a schema.

bp_requirements.title: Governance Authority - publishing a schema
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open shall enable the Governance Authority to publish and version schemas, ensuring that any resource descriptions published with one of the resource description schemas (or a version of it) within the data space adhere to the defined standards and rules, and that other types of schemas (federated search schema) can be made available.

bp_requirements.title: Governance Authority - revoking and retaining a schema
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open shall allow the Governance Authority to revoke a schema when needed and retain it.

bp_requirements.title: Governance Authority - notifying Providers about schema changes
bp_requirements.text: Simpl-Open shall notify Providers when a resource description schema is published, a new version of an existing resource description schema is published, or a resource description schema is revoked, so that Providers are aware and can, if required or relevant, adapt their resource descriptions accordingly.
